programs.name: suifft
programs.purpose: Convert complex frequency traces to real time traces with an inverse FFT.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUIFFT - fft complex frequency traces to real time traces
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Prime-factor FFT and float normalization depend on arithmetic order; output sampling is computed from d1 or dt.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program performs an inverse real FFT and adjusts frequency-domain headers.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sufft sign=1 | suifft sign=-1
suplane nt=96 ntr=4 | sufft sign=-1 | suifft sign=1

programs.name: suphasevel
programs.purpose: Compute a complex phase-velocity dispersion map from traces and their offsets.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUPHASEVEL - Multi-mode PHASE VELocity dispersion map computed

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: from header dt; errors if header dt is zero

params.name: norm
params.description: Set to 1 to normalize each input spectrum by amplitude.

params.name: tmpdir
params.default: computed: CWP_TMPDIR environment variable if set, otherwise empty string

programs.float_sensitive_notes: FFT, complex exponentials and ordered float summation affect results. Normalization divides by zero for zero spectral amplitudes; fmax can select bins beyond the allocated FFT spectrum, and more than 10000 input offsets overflow the offset array.
programs.difficulty_reason: The transform buffers a full gather and sums complex phase kernels across offsets for each frequency and velocity.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushw key=offset a=100 b=25 | suphasevel fv=500 dv=100 nv=5 fmax=0 norm=0
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushw key=offset a=100 b=25 | suphasevel fv=600 dv=50 nv=4 fmax=40 norm=1

programs.license_note: Credits state that the program was cloned from suspecfk and cite a 1998 SEG abstract.

programs.name: suradon
programs.purpose: Compute forward or inverse Radon transforms and estimate or subtract multiples.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SURADON - compute forward or reverse Radon transform or remove multiples

params.name: choose
params.description: Operation: forward, subtraction, multiple estimate, forward and inverse, or inverse for values 0 through 4.

params.name: igopt
params.description: Moveout geometry: parabolic, hyperbolic, linear, or absolute linear.

params.name: anderson
params.description: Interpret p values as reference-offset milliseconds when 1, or horizontal slowness when 0.

params.name: nwin
params.description: Number of mute-zone windows; negative values are reset to 1.

params.name: f1
params.description: Frequency where the high-frequency taper begins.

params.name: f2
params.description: Frequency where the high-frequency taper ends.

params.name: cdpkey
params.default: cdp

params.name: offkey
params.default: offset

params.name: ninterp
params.description: Traces interpolated between input traces. The parameter is read twice; the second missing-parameter default overrides the first default of 0.

params.name: xopt
params.description: Spatial derivative: differences for 1, FFT for 0; fewer than 16 traces force differences.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: FFT transforms, ordered complex sums, Toeplitz or conjugate-gradient solves, interpolation and trigonometric functions are sensitive to rounding. The selfdoc notes a freq1=0 bug; some paths can divide by zero or use invalid dimensions. The duplicated ninterp parsing changes its effective default.
programs.difficulty_reason: This is a disk-backed ensemble inversion with iterative solvers, interpolation, mute windows and multiple processing modes.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushw key=cdp,offset a=1,100 b=0,100 | suradon choose=0 ninterp=0 nxmax=16 pmin=-32 pmax=32 dp=16 f1=40 f2=60

test_cases.description: Forward and inverse linear transform with interpolation.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushw key=cdp,offset a=1,100 b=0,100 | suradon choose=3 igopt=3 ninterp=1 nxmax=16 pmin=-32 pmax=32 dp=16 f1=40 f2=60
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sushw key=cdp,offset a=1,100 b=0,100 | suradon choose=1 ninterp=0 nxmax=16 pmin=-32 pmax=64 dp=16 pmula=0 pmulb=32

programs.license_note: Credits identify John Anderson as a visitor from Mobil; references include SEG expanded abstracts.

programs.name: suslowft
programs.purpose: Compute a direct discrete Fourier transform of each real input trace.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSLOWFT - Fourier Transforms by a (SLOW) DFT algorithm (Not an FFT)

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; 0.004 if zero

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The quadratic DFT accumulates floats in order and uses sin and cos. It writes 2*nt float values but sets ns=nt, so the trace writer emits only nt values.
programs.difficulty_reason: The direct DFT requires complex arithmetic and careful handling of its unusual output length.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=4 | suslowft sign=1 dt=0.004
suplane nt=96 ntr=2 | suslowft sign=-1 dt=0.002

programs.license_note: The DFT function comments cite Numerical Recipes in C, page 406.

programs.name: suslowift
programs.purpose: Compute a direct inverse discrete Fourier transform from complex frequency samples to real traces.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSLOWIFT - Fourier Transforms by (SLOW) DFT algorithm (Not an FFT)

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; 0.004 if zero
params.description: Sampling interval used for an advisory message.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The quadratic DFT uses ordered float accumulation and trigonometric functions. It reads 2*ns floats from the trace data even though the input trace contains only ns floats, so the second half can contain stale or zero-initialized data.
programs.difficulty_reason: The direct inverse DFT uses complex arithmetic and unusual input-length assumptions.

test_cases.description: Default inverse after slow forward transform.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=4 | suslowft sign=1 | suslowift sign=-1 dt=0.004
suplane nt=64 ntr=2 | suslowft sign=-1 | suslowift sign=1 dt=0.002

programs.license_note: The code is based on suifft and its DFT function comments cite Numerical Recipes.

programs.name: suspecfk
programs.purpose: Compute the amplitude spectrum of a trace panel in frequency and spatial wavenumber.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSPECFK - F-K Fourier SPECtrum of data set

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; 0.004 if zero

params.name: dx
params.default: computed: header d2; 1.0 if zero

params.name: tmpdir
params.default: computed: CWP_TMPDIR environment variable if set, otherwise empty string

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Two-dimensional prime-factor FFTs and complex magnitudes are sensitive to floating-point evaluation and math-library behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers the full panel and performs two FFT dimensions.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | suspecfk verbose=0
suplane nt=96 ntr=12 | suspecfk dt=0.002 dx=25 verbose=1

programs.name: suspecfx
programs.purpose: Compute the frequency amplitude spectrum of each trace.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSPECFX - Fourier SPECtrum (T -> F) of traces

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; 0.004 if zero

programs.float_sensitive_notes: FFT and complex magnitude calculations can differ with arithmetic order and math libraries; the DC amplitude is halved.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program performs a padded real FFT on each trace.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | suspecfx
suplane nt=96 ntr=4 | suspecfx dt=0.002

programs.name: suspeck1k2
programs.purpose: Compute the two-dimensional spatial wavenumber amplitude spectrum of a trace panel.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUSPECK1K2 - 2D (K1,K2) Fourier SPECtrum of (x1,x2) data set

params.name: d1
params.default: computed: header d1; 1.0 if zero

params.name: d2
params.default: computed: header d2; 1.0 if zero

params.name: tmpdir
params.default: computed: CWP_TMPDIR environment variable if set, otherwise empty string

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Two-dimensional FFTs and complex magnitudes depend on floating-point operation order and math-library behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers a full panel, performs two FFT dimensions and rearranges the spectrum.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=64 ntr=8 | sushw key=trid a=30 | suspeck1k2
suplane nt=96 ntr=12 | sushw key=trid a=30 | suspeck1k2 d1=5 d2=25 verbose=1

programs.name: sust
programs.purpose: Produce a time-frequency amplitude representation using the Stockwell transform.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUST -  Outputs a time-frequency representation of seismic data via

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; errors if zero
params.description: Time sample interval; required when header dt is zero.

params.name: fmin
params.default: computed: 0.0 times Nyquist

params.name: fmax
params.default: computed: Nyquist frequency

programs.float_sensitive_notes: FFT, double Gaussian exponentials and square roots mix with float spectra. The transform writes nfft samples per row into rows allocated for nt samples, causing out-of-bounds writes when padding makes nfft greater than nt; work arrays are leaked per trace.
programs.difficulty_reason: The transform builds a separate frequency-dependent Gaussian and inverse FFT for each frequency bin.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=2 | sust dt=0.004 fmin=10 fmax=40 verbose=0
suplane nt=64 ntr=2 | sust dt=0.002 fmin=0 fmax=250 verbose=1

programs.license_note: Credits name BRGM and Adnand Bitri; the header cites Stockwell-transform publications.

programs.name: sutaup
programs.purpose: Compute forward or inverse global slant stacks in the time-space or frequency-wavenumber domain.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUTAUP - forward and inverse T-X and F-K global slant stacks

params.name: option
params.description: Select forward F-K, forward T-X, inverse F-K, or inverse T-X for values 1 through 4.

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: header dt in seconds; errors if zero

params.name: nx
params.default: computed: number of input traces

params.name: npoints
params.description: Rho-filter points for inverse T-X processing.

params.name: np
params.default: computed: number of input traces
params.description: Number of slope samples and output traces.

params.name: ntau
params.default: computed: input nt in the documented interface
params.description: Documented only; the code never reads this parameter and always uses input nt.

params.name: tmpdir
params.default: computed: CWP_TMPDIR environment variable if set, otherwise empty string

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The library slant stacks use FFTs or interpolation and ordered sums. np=1 divides by zero, and dimensions or header reads can be invalid when user-supplied nx or np differ from the trace count.
programs.difficulty_reason: Four multi-trace slant-stack modes delegate to substantial numerical library routines.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup option=1 dt=0.004 dx=25 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002 fmin=5
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup option=2 dt=0.004 dx=25 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup option=2 dt=0.004 dx=25 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002 | sutaup option=4 dt=0.004 dx=25 nx=8 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002 npoints=11
suplane nt=128 ntr=8 | sutaup option=1 dt=0.004 dx=25 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002 | sutaup option=3 dt=0.004 dx=25 nx=8 np=8 pmin=-0.002 pmax=0.002 fmin=5

programs.license_note: The header references an SEG Press slant-stack volume.

programs.name: suwfft
programs.purpose: Flatten each trace's FFT amplitude spectrum using weighted neighboring amplitudes.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUWFFT - Weighted amplitude FFT with spectrum flattening 0->Nyquist

params.name: sign
params.description: FFT exponent sign; must be 1 or -1.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The FFT and amplitude divisions are rounding-sensitive. The code reads ct[-1] and ct[nf] when computing boundary weights; its i==nf condition is unreachable, and zero amplitudes cause division by zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program performs an FFT and frequency-bin weighting with unsafe boundary accesses.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suwfft sign=1 verbose=0 w0=0.75 w1=1 w2=0.75
suplane nt=96 ntr=4 | suwfft sign=-1 verbose=0 w0=0 w1=1 w2=0

programs.license_note: Credits describe the concept as coming from Bassel Al-Moughraby's University of Tulsa PhD thesis.

programs.name: suzerophase
programs.purpose: Replace each trace's phase spectrum to produce a zero-phase equivalent centered at a chosen time.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUZEROPHASE - convert input to zero phase equivalent

params.name: dt
params.default: computed: seismic header dt or nonseismic header d1; if zero, supplied dt or 0.004
params.description: Sampling interval is consulted only when the selected header interval is zero.

params.name: t0
params.description: Peak time used in the spectral phase and output delay.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Complex FFT, magnitude, sine and cosine calculations and float scaling are sensitive to operation order and math-library behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program performs forward and inverse complex FFTs and reconstructs a Hermitian phase spectrum.

test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=4 | suzerophase t0=1 verbose=0
suplane nt=96 ntr=4 | suzerophase t0=0.1 verbose=1

programs.license_note: Credits identify Bruce VerWest and the SEAM project.
